subject: Borealis — technical session planning and calendar options
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Borealis — technical session planning and calendar options

Hi Elena —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and a proposed path to get you into a hands-on technical session with the ML/infra team. We heard that Borealis' immediate priorities are: reducing per-request latency during peak inference, clarifying data isolation for PII, and validating throughput at 5–10 TPS for your 2k token average requests.

Proposed next step: a 60–90 minute technical session (engineers + infra + security) to:
- review current workload profile and sequence-length distribution
- validate model/quantization options and expected unit cost
- run a short capacity/latency Q&A and discuss fallback routing

Suggested windows (all PT):
- Tue 16 Feb, 10:00–11:15 (75m)
- Wed 17 Feb, 08:00–09:15 (75m)
- Thu 18 Feb, 13:00–14:30 (90m)

Please let me know which of these work or propose two alternatives. Also confirm attendees from your side (we recommend an ML lead, infra/ops, and a security/compliance contact).

Attaching a short discovery-notes.pdf and a one-page pre-read that outlines what the session will include.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: discovery-notes.pdf, pre-read-redwood-inference.pdf

Subject: Re: Borealis — technical session planning and calendar options

Thanks, Ben —

Appreciate the recap. The goals you listed match our priorities. A couple quick asks before we lock a time:
1) Can you include our Head of Security (Diego Soto) on the session? He'll need a short compliance-focused segment (15–20m) on data residency and audit logs.
2) We prefer morning PT slots but are flexible. Wed 17 Feb at 08:00 PT looks promising for most of our team.
3) Will you be able to record the session and share slides/notes for stakeholders who cannot make it?

Attendees from Borealis: Elena Morales (you@contact), Diego Soto (security). I'll add a third person if my ML lead confirms.

Thanks — Elena

I can join Wed 17 Feb 08:00 PT and run the infra portion. We'll spin up a 4-GPU test pool with the customer's seq-length profile and a representative model (recommended quantized variant) so we can show KV-cache warmup effects and steady-state latency. Plan: 20m walkthrough of infra and perf dashboard, 25–30m Q&A/troubleshooting, 15–20m on security/compliance (Diego), and 10–15m for next steps and mutual action items.

Adding an agenda item for KV cache warmup / latency SLOs as Elena flagged latency concerns. I'll attach a short capacity-plan.xlsx with the node sizes we propose.
